subject.name: NodeRoom capture path, after the note-surface fix — palette 'Capture a thought' plus the wall Capture button
subject.surface: The same route as the baseline receipt (score-noderoom-capture-path-capture-always-armed-before), re-scored after feat/note-surface-dna added a capture command to the ctrl/cmd+K palette: buildWallCapture (src/ui/RoomShell.tsx) creates an empty wall capture through the CAS spine, opens the wall, and focuses the new post-it's contentEditable.
subject.evidenceRef: source, noderoom branch feat/note-surface-dna: RoomShell.tsx buildWallCapture + capture-thought palette action (listed first), tests/captureThought.test.ts (4 scenario tests, passing: empty-text op, 50-capture burst, color cycle, CAS replay refusal)

appliesWhenSatisfied: the surface's value depends on catching transient input: unchanged from the baseline receipt

doesNotApplyWhenChecked.clause: compliance-bound intake where classification is legally prior (the trust-surfaces contract governs those forms)
doesNotApplyWhenChecked.note: Unchanged: wall captures are free-text post-its with no classification requirement, and the new palette command asks nothing.

anchors.0: no capture affordance exists anywhere without opening a specific artifact, and no global entry point exists at all
anchors.1: a single global entry point (the palette keystroke) exists, but it lists no capture command — capture still sits behind destination navigation, in the shape of Evernote's choose-first gate (obs-evernote-contrast/f4)
anchors.2: the global entry point carries a capture command, but it asks a classification question — type, destination, color — before accepting text
anchors.3: the global keystroke path arms a text-ready capture with no classification question; a persistent mobile capture affordance is absent (short of obs-mew-stream/f6)
anchors.4: one global keystroke on desktop plus a persistent floating control on mobile, and neither asks anything before the first keystroke (obs-mew-stream/f4, f6)

criteria.question: Is capture reachable from every state via one global keystroke?

citations.note: Mew's cmd+k adds the note directly to the top of the stream. NodeRoom's ctrl/cmd+K now lists 'Capture a thought' first, so the path is keystroke, Enter (the first row is preselected), typing — one selection step more than Mew's direct add, from any state where the user is not already mid-typing (the palette deliberately never steals ctrl/cmd+K from a text field).

criteria.finding: One keystroke and one Enter from every non-typing state. The residual selection step and the textEntryIsActive guard keep this short of Mew's direct-add fact.

criteria.question: Does the path to capture ask a classification question before accepting text?

citations.note: The Evernote gate — choose a destination type before capturing — is no longer paid: the command picks the wall itself, presets position and color, creates the element with empty text, and focuses its contentEditable. Nothing is asked between intent and caret.

Deferring classification to after the thought is safe is the mechanism this rule names; the wall's existing edit affordances (color, position, deletion) remain available after capture. The caret-landing is a best-effort two-frame focus; in convex mode a slow round-trip can leave the capture created but unfocused, which is a caveat on arming, not on capture.

criteria.finding: Zero classification questions before the first keystroke. Scenario tests pin the contract: empty text, preset placement, CAS create, burst-safe ids.

criteria.question: Does a persistent floating capture control exist on mobile?

citations.note: Unchanged from baseline: the compact layout gained nothing. A palette keystroke is not a mobile affordance — there is no hardware ctrl/cmd+K on a phone — and this fix did not attempt one.

criteria.finding: Still absent, still zero. Recorded unimproved; closing it is a separate change with its own layout consequences, not a side effect this task should smuggle in.

scoreBasis: Ladder: the subject sits at the highest anchor it fully satisfies. The desktop path now arms a text-ready capture with no classification (anchor 3's condition); c3's mobile absence keeps anchor 4 closed.
notScored: Capture into the chat composer — unchanged, a different record type.
Keystroke-to-caret latency in convex mode — the two-frame focus is best-effort and was not measured against a live backend.
Whether users discover the palette command — discoverability is an audience-task question (M3) no evidence here can answer.
The wall's spatial canvas behavior after many palette captures stack at x:0 y:0 — a layout question outside this rule's licence.
boundary: Scored from source on branch feat/note-surface-dna plus its passing scenario tests, not from a recorded user session. The click-count claims trace the palette code path by hand; the focus claim is implemented but unverified against a running browser in this receipt.
